dataset.name: real WANDS catalog (42,994 products), same 7 category_depth_1 checkpoints as P6A-E00/P6B-E00/P6C-E00/P6C-E01

engine_config.solr: Apache Solr 9.10.1, wands_bench core, re-queried same session, reused for both native comparisons

headline_result.correctness_gate: unit test: exact BTreeMap match vs facet_counts_by_scan across full/filtered/empty/never-indexed inputs; real-data: 21/21 exact top-50-facet matches against the live Solr wands_bench core across 3 runs, 0 mismatches
headline_result.ordinal_vs_solr_7_of_7_checkpoints: faster at every checkpoint, 5.2x-69.8x, no exceptions
headline_result.finding: the facet crossover this project has repeatedly measured (Phase 5, 6A, 6B, P6C-E00) was a property of naive per-candidate scanning specifically (a full attribute-map clone per candidate), not an inherent ceiling on commerce-native's own architecture; given a comparably specialized ordinal/dictionary-based counting strategy, commerce-native substantially exceeds both Solr and Lucene's own margin over Solr (P6C-E01: up to 3.0x, still trailing at 2 checkpoints)
headline_result.named_limitation: only color facet tested (not product_class or others); only WANDS 1x scale (not the Phase 6B scale ladder); memory cost of new dictionary/column structures estimated, not measured; MultiEnum attributes not supported by the ordinal path; no real query-serving path wired to prefer this method yet
